skill.name: canvas-design
skill.description: Create original visual art as PNG or PDF files using a written design philosophy, refined composition, and bundled font choices.
skill.summary: Turn a design brief into a visual philosophy and a polished static canvas artifact.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Open Font License text and Markdown formatting in SKILL.md. The bundled TTF files are confirmed low-severity metadata findings because they are binary assets, and one medium semantic issue remains for open-ended font downloads.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer the bundled canvas-fonts directory. If more fonts are needed, require user confirmation and use trusted sources with license and integrity checks.

remediation.issue: Bundled binary font assets require manual review
remediation.suggestion: Document the source and license for each bundled font, and keep checksums so future updates can be verified.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Font Download Instruction
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs the agent to "Download and use whatever fonts are needed" without limiting sources, requiring confirmation, or verifying font integrity. This can cause network access and introduce untrusted font files into generated work.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and directly allows open-ended font downloads. No malicious URL or command is present, so medium severity is appropriate.

content.value_statement: Static visual pieces often need a clear art direction before execution. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create a design philosophy and express it as PNG or PDF artwork.
actual_capabilities: Creates a written visual philosophy before producing the final artwork.
Guides generation of single-page PNG or PDF design artifacts.
Uses composition, color, spacing, typography, and repeated visual systems as core design tools.
Supports subtle conceptual references in abstract or poster-like compositions.
Encourages second-pass refinement for alignment, margins, text fit, and visual polish.
Includes a bundled font directory for typography choices.
limitations: It is focused on static visual artifacts, not interactive interfaces or motion graphics.
It does not provide a deterministic rendering engine or exact layout guarantees by itself.
It may need user review for copyright, brand, and licensing requirements.
External font downloads should be avoided unless the user approves a trusted source.

use_cases.title: Event Poster Concept
use_cases.description: Create a polished poster with a strong visual language, minimal text, and careful typography.

use_cases.title: Editorial Art Direction
use_cases.description: Develop an abstract visual philosophy that can guide a magazine cover or feature image.

use_cases.title: Presentation Cover Artwork
use_cases.description: Produce a refined title page or standalone visual for a report, pitch, or internal showcase.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Poster
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one static design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a single-page poster as a PNG for [event or topic]. Use minimal text, strong visual hierarchy, and a refined design philosophy.

prompt_templates.title: Brand Mood Piece
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PDF visual mood piece for [brand or project]. Use [colors], [tone], and sparse typography. Include the design philosophy as a Markdown file.

prompt_templates.title: Subtle Reference Artwork
prompt_templates.prompt: Create abstract canvas art for [subject]. Hide a subtle reference to [specific idea] through form, rhythm, color, or structure without explaining it directly.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Page Art Series
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a cohesive set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a cohesive three-page PDF art series for [theme]. Each page should use the same design philosophy but show a distinct visual variation.

output_examples.input: Create a poster for a late-night architecture lecture about invisible cities.
output_examples.output: A one-page PNG poster with dense map-like linework, sparse lecture details, restrained typography, and a matching design philosophy document.

output_examples.input: Design a cover image for a product strategy report about reliable systems.
output_examples.output: A polished PDF cover using modular grids, precise spacing, quiet labels, and a visual language based on engineered calm.

output_examples.input: Make abstract artwork for a music release with a hidden reference to analog tape.
output_examples.output: A static artwork file with layered bands, calibrated texture, minimal title text, and subtle reel-inspired composition cues.

best_practices: Provide the intended format, audience, subject, and any required text before generation.
Name constraints such as colors, dimensions, brand rules, and prohibited styles early.
Review the first output for margins, overlap, readability, and license-sensitive assets.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for direct imitation of living artists, copyrighted covers, or protected brand artwork.
Do not overload the design with long paragraphs or dense explanatory text.
Do not request unapproved external font downloads or unknown asset sources.

faq.question: What files can this skill create?
faq.answer: It is designed for Markdown design philosophy files and static PNG or PDF artwork.

faq.question: Does it copy existing artists?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly directs original visual designs and avoids copying existing artists.

faq.question: Can it use custom fonts?
faq.answer: It includes bundled fonts. New font downloads should use trusted sources and user approval.

faq.question: Is this useful for UI design?
faq.answer: It is better for posters, covers, art pieces, and static visual compositions than app interfaces.

faq.question: Can I request multiple pages?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes guidance for creating a cohesive multi-page PDF or image set.

faq.question: What should I include in my prompt?
faq.answer: Include the subject, format, audience, required text, visual tone, and any asset or license constraints.
